Description

RAS proteins (HRAS, KRAS, NRAS) are small GTPases anchored on the inner face of the plasma membrane, active when they hold GTP and inactive when they hold GDP. The exchange factor SOS1, brought to the activated receptor by the adaptor GRB2, opens the nucleotide pocket of RAS so that GDP leaves and the more abundant GTP binds [1-3]. RAS hydrolyses GTP slowly on its own. The GTPase-activating proteins p120GAP (RASA1) and neurofibromin (NF1) insert an arginine into its active site and speed its hydrolysis, which returns RAS to its GDP-bound state [4-7]. The oncogenic mutations at glycine 12 and glutamine 61 make RAS resistant to this acceleration, so it stays loaded with GTP [4, 5].
